messages:
lee: Noticed a reproducible customer regression: after a prefix gets demoted then quickly rehydrated on a different node, some in-flight writes from the old owner win and stomp the fresh backend state.
tasha: Oof. Is that the 'stale-owner-apply' we've talked about before?
lee: Similar but manifests differently. Rehydrate brings payload+ttl but we don't carry an ownership epoch. Old owner had a pending ack write which races the rehydrate+write-back. If old owner applies after rehydrate, we end up with stale payload and later eviction vs expectation.
anya: So concrete invariant: once a prefix is demoted and another node rehydrates, we must ensure any write from previous ownership with lower epoch cannot be applied. We need epoch on the cache entry and require write's epoch >= current epoch.
jon: That implies writesets must include an owner_epoch. Do we already have anything like that in the handshake? I thought leases had epoch ids but maybe not surfaced to apply path.
asha: (typo) I mean tasha: We have lease_token but it's not monotonic across claim transfers; it is opaque. We need an explicit claim_epoch counter that increments on handoff.
lee: Proposal:
- Add claim_epoch (u64) to ownership handshake and persisted with cached entry.
- Rehydrate carries backend_epoch (if backend tracks it) and we set local_epoch = max(claim_epoch_from_handshake, backend_epoch) depending on trust.
- All mutating ops (apply/update/evict-ack) require check: op_epoch >= local_epoch else reject and emit metric.
anya: For correctness I'd prefer the cache exclusively uses claim_epoch from runtime handshakes as the authority for local ordering. Backend_epoch is nice-safety but backend might not update on every write. If backend has EPOCH, we can compare and emit warnings but not rely on it.
jon: Also need to consider multi-tenant shared slab: claim_epoch needs to be compact (u64 ok) and we should encode in cache binary as a small header to avoid memory blowup.
tasha: Operationally we should be able to inspect per-prefix epoch in admin UI and have an alert when a write is rejected due to epoch_mismatch. That will help debug.
lee: Edgecases: what about soft-evict grace windows? If prefix is soft-evicted and then immediately rehydrated by same node, epoch should not bump. Only bump on handoff to different owner.
anya: Right. handshake message should include previous_owner_id; if new owner == previous_owner, keep epoch. else epoch = previous_epoch + 1. We'll add deterministic increment in the sequencer.
jon: Implementation steps:
1) runtime: extend ownership proto: claim_epoch (optional u64), previous_owner_id (string)
2) cache entry: store claim_epoch and check on apply
3) write path: require writer supplies op_epoch (from its active lease) else reject
4) rehydrate: set claim_epoch from handshake; emit metric rehydrate_epoch_delta = new_epoch - old_epoch
5) add admin column and logs for rejected-applies
6) tests: unit for epoch enforcement, integration for demote->rehydrate->stale-write repro
7) rollout: server feature flag behind canary on dedicated clusters
tasha: Metrics/alerts:
- prefix_apply_rejected_total{reason="epoch_mismatch"}
- prefix_claim_epoch_gauge (per-prefix)
- rehydrate_epoch_delta_histogram
- alert: high rate of prefix_apply_rejected_total for a prefix -> throttle writes and investigate
lee: One more thing: eviction ordering. If a stale write is rejected but had also scheduled an eviction, we must ensure the eviction doesn't run based on that stale command. Eviction tasks must include op_epoch and be gated the same way.
anya: Good catch. We'll treat evict as a mutating op with epoch checks. Also add a tombstone marker only when epoch check passes.
jon: Backwards compatibility: encode optional claim_epoch in proto. Older nodes will treat absent as epoch=0 and still work; but that allows possible regressions during mixed-version rollout. So we must coordinate rollout: owners should be updated before potential writers. Add rollout doc.
asha: (again typo) tasha: Can we simulate mixed-version in our test harness? We should run mixed-runtime test to ensure safe upgrade path.
lee: Yes, ANYA can add to simulator.
anya: I'll add mixed-version scenarios and a canary plan. Also add a smoke test that intentionally replays the stale-owner-apply and expects rejection.
jon: Punting to tickets: INF-501: proto+runtime change, INF-502: cache checks+eviction gating, INF-503: metrics+dashboards, INF-504: simulator+mixed-version tests, INF-505: admin UI column.
lee: I'll attach traces from the customer repro to INF-501.
deploy-bot: reminder: update API compatibility doc if you change protos -> see infra-guidelines.md
lee: Anyone object to this plan?
tasha: No objections from me. Important to prevent data regressions.
anya: LGTM, will start simulator work tomorrow.
jon: LGTM, I'll scope the dashboards.
lee: Great. I'll write up a short RFC follow-up and reference tickets. Thanks everyone.
